department: Joint Ph.D. Program in Biomedical Engineering (NJIT with Rutgers Newark Health Science Campus)

deadline.value: The joint program page gives no application deadline.

gre_general.value: The biomedical engineering PhD requires the GRE, while the Newark College of Engineering says the GRE is optional.
gre_general.quote: The GRE is required for all applicants, and TOEFL is required for all international students.

also.quote: Newark College of Engineering - GRE optional but strongly recommended for all MS and PhD applicants

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: The page does not say whether a supervisor must agree before admission.

funding.value: The page says teaching assistantships and fellowships are limited, without a stated share of funded students.

entry_route.value: Students may come with a bachelor's degree and enter directly, or with a master's degree.
entry_route.quote: Students may also be admitted directly to the Joint Degree Program after earning a B.S. or B.A. degree.

also.quote: Applicants are recommended to have a minimum G.P.A of 3.5 in their most recent degree (B.S. or M.S.)

notes: Admission is through a joint committee; the GRE rule conflicts between the program page and the graduate school's college rule.
name: Ph.D. in Biomedical Engineering (joint with Rutgers)
